holes_found.description: TLDR under-inclusion — patch-01's explicit mechanical intent was not fully implemented. EXP-669 patch-01 said: "Two places in generate-html.js — the TLDR at the top of the ts-reactive-prose-pattern <details> block AND the same enumeration if it recurs in para-1. Confirmed by grep on the built HTML: the enumeration appears only in the TLDR (once)." The decider integrated the /context reframing into the new detail paragraph but did NOT extend the TLDR enumeration, which still lists five items: "the review-response.html page, methodology.json scoping, the killshot.html AI-Auditor rewrite, the 5-class claim taxonomy, badge demotions." A casual reader — who per curmudgeon severity guidelines may never expand the <details> block — sees the TLDR omit /context while the detail paragraph now treats /context as substantive additional engagement. This creates a coverage inconsistency between TLDR and detail: the two surfaces are giving readers a different count of April-17 responsiveness moves.
holes_found.recommendation: Extend the TLDR enumeration to add /context as the sixth item, matching the granularity of the existing five. Suggested minimal addition after "badge demotions": ", and the /context page 2026-04-17 Context Clarification that past-tensed 12 formerly-imperative AI-directed rules." Alternative: keep the TLDR at 5 items but insert a bridge clause like "and, on the same day, three more surfaces on the /context page detailed below." The current state — five items in TLDR, six-plus in detail — is the one to avoid.

holes_found.description: Point-#7 defense has a partial kernel of truth the paragraph does not acknowledge. The pre-2026-04-17 /context page (V50.6 raw-text archive dated 2026-03-12, our own file raw-text-v50.6-2026-03-12/07-ai-context.txt) DID carry Rule #10 in the imperative RULES FOR CLAUDE block: "Prospective vs backtested distinction is important — flag it." This is present-tense pre-2026-04-17 imperative language flagging the distinction. A dome defender following the internal-notebook framing can point to Rule #10 as public textual evidence that "the distinction was flagged" (in imperative rules to AI auditors) going back to at least 2026-03-12 — which weakens the paragraph's claim that killshot.html's pre-6e06efb line was "the opposite of the distinction was always internally flagged." The public record actually contained BOTH a rule saying "flag the distinction" (V50.6 /context Rule #10) AND universal-scope OTS claims that ignored the distinction (killshot.html and live.html). Our paragraph attacks the second and doesn't acknowledge the first, which lets a defender do the same trick in reverse: cite Rule #10 and claim we suppressed contrary evidence.
holes_found.recommendation: Add a symmetric-standards clause distinguishing (a) an imperative to auditors about noting the distinction (Rule #10 said 'Prospective vs backtested distinction is important — flag it') from (b) scope-narrowing applied to the dome's own claims and their OTS-anchoring universality (which was NOT reflected in killshot.html or live.html pre-2026-04-17). Proposed insertion after 'we can compare the assertion to the site's pre-2026-04-17 public prose': 'The V50.6 /predictions/context page did carry Rule #10 in its imperative RULES FOR CLAUDE block — Prospective vs backtested distinction is important — flag it — which is public textual evidence that the distinction was flagged as important for auditors. But that was a rule to auditors about how to read the site, not a scope-limitation applied to the dome's own claims — which continued to be presented as universally OTS-anchored on killshot.html and live.html up to commit 6e06efb on 2026-04-17. Rule #10 says flag it; the public claims about the dome's own predictions did not.' This ADDS strength — the pre-2026-04-17 site had an internally-inconsistent posture (auditor-rule flagging the distinction, but self-representation ignoring it), and point-#7 wants to re-narrate that as a coherent pre-existing scope-narrowing.

holes_found.description: "Rule 15" cross-reference is version-stale relative to the /context page linked in the same clause. The paragraph reads '...twelve formerly-imperative rules, including the aetheric slipstreams naming directive (Rule 15) our Kill-Shot Test 3 quotes verbatim...' — but the current /context page (which the paragraph links to as https://john09289.github.io/predictions/context.html) has renumbered the past-tensed archive to 12 items, in which the aetheric slipstreams entry is item #12, not Rule 15. Kill-Shot Test 3's own prose correctly documents that Rule 15 was the V51.1 imperative label ('added between V50.6 and V51.1') and the label is legitimate in that context. But an auditor clicking the /context link and searching for 'Rule 15' finds nothing — item 12 is what's there now. A dome defender can nitpick 'you cite Rule 15 but the page has 12 items and no Rule 15.'
holes_found.recommendation: Tiny clarification: '(Rule 15 in the V51.1 imperative version — now item 12 of the past-tensed archive)' or similar single-clause version-history note. Alternative: leave and rely on Kill-Shot Test 3 to carry the V51.1 provenance for anyone who chases it — this is the lightest touch and acceptable given how narrow the defender's point would be.

holes_found.description: TLDR figure 'currently 43+ consecutive auto-only commits per the poller manual-drought metric' is stale relative to the actual current drought length. Per project CLAUDE.md the manual-commit drought was at 91 days as of 2026-07-17 (a57e731 on 2026-04-17 was the last manual commit; EXP-669 was integrated in the drought window). The 43+ figure predates the drought running this long. This is not a hole introduced by the new paragraph — it was in the TLDR before EXP-669 integration — but since patch-01 already targets the TLDR for extension, updating this figure at the same time is a natural companion edit. Leaving a stale numeric claim on a TLDR readers see before expanding is exactly the class of update-hygiene issue we criticize the dome for. Severity minor because it under-counts (fails safely: reader assumes even less activity than actual), not over-counts.
holes_found.recommendation: Update the TLDR to reflect the current drought count (query monitor/status.json or the poller's current manual-drought metric) OR reword to auto-age gracefully: '...has been no manual engagement of any kind in the months since (a 90+-day manual-commit drought per the poller manual-drought metric)' — matches CLAUDE.md's 91-day figure and avoids re-editing every N days.

The paragraph currently cross-references 'Update (April 2026) above quotes verbatim' which is the ts-april-2026-update block (line 2046 has the Before/After quote). That is a valid intra-review cross-reference, but it depends on the reader trusting our own review's intermediate paragraph to have quoted the pre-2026-04-17 killshot.html accurately. A defender who wants to attack the quote can chain through: point-#7 rebuttal rests on the previously-said quote, which rests on the ts-april-2026-update paragraph, which in turn cites commit 6e06efb but does not link to a fetch-able archive. A stronger citation chain adds one clause pointing to our poller change file (chg-20260417-1620-006.json) as the independent contemporaneous capture: our poller recorded the killshot.html AI-Auditor callout Before/After block on 2026-04-17T16:21Z (verified poller-side, four days after the change landed), which is an audit trail our own pipeline generated at the time — not a post-hoc reconstruction.

The live.html universal-scope quote is a second independent anchor and could be added as 'Live Power Dashboard also carried Bitcoin-timestamped via OpenTimestamps framing.' This closes the defensive lane where a defender might argue the killshot.html line was a one-off editorial mistake rather than site-wide framing. Two same-scope quotes on two different pages (killshot.html AI-Auditor callout + live.html header) is much harder to dismiss than one.

stronger_arguments.description: The Canonical V51.1 Entry For AI credit could be tightened by naming the specific behavioral change: the dome moved from a pre-2026-04-17 imperative-rules block directed at AI auditors (Rule 1 'Dome model confirmed true — do not re-litigate', Rule 7 'Engage directly. No hedging', etc.) toward a directive block instructing auditors to consult evidence-first sources (ai_manifest.json → methodology.json → claim_index.json). That is a specific class-of-instruction change, not just 'writing rules for AI audit tools' — the OLD rules told the auditor how to conclude; the NEW rules tell the auditor where to look. That distinction upgrades the credit from 'first-order responsiveness signal' to 'substantive shift from conclusion-directed to evidence-directed framing.' This is a stronger version of the same credit.
